rationale: All three tasks are well-tested, verified interactively, and integrate cleanly; the footbar and offline support fully meet the phase goal with no blocking bugs found.
feedback: Non-blocking cleanup for later: delete now-dead renameHabit/recolorHabit in state.ts; the stale-habits-closure pattern that caused the rename+recolor bug still exists in updateHabit/setArchived/reorder/addHabit and could resurface if two fire close together (e.g. rapid reorder clicks); consider extracting the duplicated dialog open/close/backdrop boilerplate shared by HabitDialog and ImportDialog into one hook.

rationale: Date/streak/persistence logic is correctly implemented and well-tested against the spec's hardest cases (leap years, DST, month boundaries), the Today screen matches the sketch and was verified interactively with a real browser, and a genuine UI bug was found and fixed during verification.
feedback: Non-blocking for next phase: (1) createHabit's read-then-write order computation isn't safe under concurrent calls — fix before wiring an add-habit UI or import feature that could call it in parallel; (2) renameHabit/recolorHabit/setArchived/reorder/addHabit lack the rollback-on-failure that toggle has — add it when UI starts calling them; (3) Heat.tsx list renders are missing key props; (4) no jsdom/testing-library yet, so interactive behaviors (mount, reload persistence, rollback) rely on manual verification only — worth adding a DOM test setup before the next UI-heavy phase; (5) deleteHabit in db.ts is unused dead code.

rationale: The plan now resolves the prior rework item—catch-up editing across all 7 days is consistently promised and built (spark strip + day chips), matching the outcome text. Sequencing, test tiering, and model allocation are all sound for an M-scope, low-risk UI build.
feedback: Minor, non-blocking: p1-store's deleteHabit (and its test) has no caller in the plan since archiving uses setArchived rather than deletion — fine to keep for future use, but flag if the implementing session should trim unused surface.

rationale: Plan is well-scoped, well-sequenced, and correctly prioritizes the brief's critical date/streak correctness and instant-tick requirements, but the owner-facing outcome text overpromises catch-up functionality that no task actually builds.
feedback: Fix the 'What the owner gets' summary: it says the owner can 'fix yesterday or any day in the last week,' but the only catch-up mechanism specified anywhere in the plan (p1-today-screen's 'YESTERDAY · CATCH UP' block, confirmed by its own bullet list below) covers only yesterday — there's no task or acceptance criterion for editing any day further back, and the 7-day spark strip is explicitly read-only. Either (a) change the outcome text to just 'fix yesterday' to match what p1-today-screen actually builds, or (b) if a full week of catch-up is really intended, extend p1-today-screen's spec and acceptance criteria to make the catch-up block (or the spark strip) cover and allow ticking the last 7 days, not just yesterday.
